clue.text: Problem, in a way, with trade? Then improvise

parts.note: to traffic is to trade, especially in illicit goods
musicians jam when they improvise together

explanation.surface: A trader wonders whether a business problem calls for a spot of improvisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' means on a road, so the definition is a problem met on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up of vehicles is a familiar problem on a road, which is what 'a way' means here.

clue.text: Fool grasps nothing, namely

indicators.note: one word holding another inside it is said to grasp it

parts.note: a twit is a fool
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An idiot clutches at nothing, that is to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are formal ways of introducing a specific explanation, like 'that is to say'.

clue.text: Form of rule as yet without extravagance

indicators.note: a new form of the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of governance so far marked by thrift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' rearranges the nine letters of RULE AS YET.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a plain, frugal, unadorned manner is acting without extravagance.

clue.text: Provided gloss in bilingual edition

parts.note: a book in two languages could be French-Polish

explanation.surface: A two-language edition came with a glossary of terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gloss' suggests annotation in a book, but it is the shine on furniture: French polish is a shellac finish for wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying a shellac finish to wood gave it a high shine, a gloss.

clue.text: Sails south to see how the land lies

definitions.text: to see how the land lies

parts.note: sails are made of canvas, which stands for them

explanation.surface: A sailor heads south to survey the coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: Canvassing is sounding out opinion, as a campaigner does door to door.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvassing voters is a way to gauge opinion and find out the general situation before acting.

clue.text: Mentor giving a duke means to save face

parts.note: a visor is a shield that protects the face

explanation.surface: A counsellor helps an aristocrat avoid embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save face' reads as avoiding humiliation, but here it is literal protection of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusted counsellor who guides someone is a mentor.

clue.text: Characters in front of queue, say, highly placed

definitions.text: Characters in front of queue, say
definitions.meaning: queue sounds like the letter Q, and the letters ahead of Q in the alphabet run from A to P
positioned on the top of something

explanation.walkthrough: 'queue, say' is the letter Q heard aloud; the run of the alphabet before it is A to P, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resting on top of another thing is up high, and the alphabet before Q runs A to P.

clue.text: Teach tricks to cats and dogs after short time

indicators.note: the rain piece is placed after the time piece

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
raining cats and dogs is heavy rain, so the phrase stands for rain

explanation.surface: Someone schools pets in tricks within a brief spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cats and dogs' looks like the pets being taught, but it is the idiom for heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaching an animal in tricks is drilling or schooling it.

clue.text: Useless member of team, one transferred by coach, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a team member who contributes nothing and is carried by the others
someone carried on a bus or coach journey

explanation.definitionFit: A freeloader in a team is carried like a rider on a bus, and a coach traveller is literally a rider.

clue.text: Dramatic scenes involving perfect groom, or a best man?

definitions.meaning: a stage play by Oscar Wilde whose title describes a perfect spouse
the finest possible partner a bride could marry

explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde's comedy is titled with this phrase, and literally a flawless spouse is the best man to marry.

clue.text: Partnership behind American film

parts.note: two partners together speak of themselves as we
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A business partnership backs a Hollywood picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' suggests a position after something, but it is a noun: the back part of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy picture set in the American frontier is a genre of film.

clue.text: Destructive types in youth reversing into vehicles

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: vans are vehicles

indicators.note: the young person's word is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: Young tearaways back into parked cars.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures joyriders backing into parked cars; in fact 'reversing' acts on the word for a young man, and 'into' puts the result inside the vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooligans who wreck property are destructive people, named after a Germanic tribe that sacked Rome.

clue.text: People having religious authority that is concealing corrupt core

indicators.note: one word hides another within it

parts.note: that is contracts to that's

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Religious rulers hiding a rotten heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' looks like a link phrase but supplies its own contraction, and 'corrupt' scrambles the letters of core before they go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who rule in the name of God hold religious authority over a state.

clue.text: Writer of poetry performed for audience

indicators.note: words for an audience are heard rather than read

parts.note: a play that has been done has been performed

explanation.surface: A poet's work was staged for the public.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne was an English metaphysical poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was a seventeenth-century English poet.

clue.text: Clean up in gambling event

definitions.meaning: to brush away dirt, or to win everything
a lottery-style draw where stakes are pooled and the winner takes all

explanation.definitionFit: You brush a floor to clear it, and a pooled bet such as one on a horse race is also so named.

clue.text: Not always the full amount reported by newspaper

indicators.note: reported speech is heard, so a word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a sum is a total
The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: A paper's coverage gives only part of the total.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens occasionally does not happen always.

clue.text: Displaced emigrants moving en masse

indicators.note: displaced letters are moved into new positions

explanation.surface: Uprooted migrants travel together in great numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowds flowing in a continuous mass are pouring along, a common verb for moving in great numbers.

clue.text: Something newly conceived — of necessity, a child?

definitions.meaning: the proverb says necessity is its mother

explanation.definitionFit: A new contrivance is something devised, and the proverb calls such a creation the offspring of necessity.

clue.text: Tree bark used by settlers

definitions.meaning: a name for the hawthorn, which blossoms in May
the ship that carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620

explanation.definitionFit: The hawthorn tree is called by this name, and it was also the Pilgrims' ship; a bark is a sailing vessel.

clue.text: Onlooker caught in middle of the war, unfortunately

indicators.note: one letter is placed at the centre of the other piece
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bystander was trapped amid the fighting, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges THE WAR into WATHER, and 'in middle of' puts C at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is someone who observes.

clue.text: Carnival site, from our perspective, is disorderly

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosts a famous carnival
from our point of view is to us

explanation.surface: In our view the carnival city is wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly, rowdy behaviour is wild and lawless.

clue.text: What some cross-channel craft do in south coast resort? Right

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town on England's south coast beside Brighton

explanation.surface: Asking what ferries crossing to France do at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hovercraft once crossed the English Channel; they float on a cushion of air.
explanation.definitionFit: Hovercraft float just above the water on an air cushion.

clue.text: Switch pieces of Italian food for Spanish food

indicators.note: the two parts of the word swap places

parts.note: pasta is an Italian staple

explanation.surface: Swapping Italian dishes for Spanish ones on a menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch pieces of' splits PASTA into PAS and TA and swaps them.
explanation.definitionFit: Small savoury dishes served with drinks are a Spanish tradition.

clue.text: Nut from California incarcerated there

annotationWithheld.why: 'Nut from California incarcerated there' (5): CA inside PEN, but no clue word gives PEN apart from 'incarcerated', which would have to be both the pen and the container indicator.

clue.text: Large numbers as maximum limits

definitions.meaning: great quantities, many hundreds and more
the outer letters of the word maximum are M and M, and M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.definitionFit: Multiples of a thousand are big quantities, and the letters M bounding 'maximum' each stand for a thousand.

clue.text: In reserved way, have fling with heartless lady

parts.note: to shy is to fling or throw

indicators.note: a word without its heart keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A coy woman has a timid affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have fling' suggests a romance, but to shy is to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something bashfully or timidly is behaving in a reserved manner.

clue.text: Scientist accepting gamble in play with tragic results

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: Ernst Mach was an Austrian physicist
a bet is a gamble

explanation.surface: A researcher's wager in a drama goes badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Scottish tragedy is a play ending in many deaths.

clue.text: Unclear quality of work a financial centre goes after

indicators.note: the second part follows the first

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a work
the City of London is the financial district

explanation.surface: A banker pursues a vague piece of business.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaqueness, the state of being cloudy or obscure, is lack of clarity.

clue.text: Succeed in putting son in kindergarten, originally

indicators.note: the original letter is the first one of the word

explanation.surface: A parent manages to get their boy into nursery school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' looks like placing a child, but it is golf: holing a putt.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to hole a ball is to succeed at a putt.

clue.text: Office at the top in quiet dwelling

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music
a residency is a dwelling place

explanation.surface: The top job comes with a peaceful official home.
explanation.definitionFit: The post of head of state or chair is the highest position.
